prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1253; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- It is not fully clear where in the vehicle the claimant was sitting.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant, who reports being hit on the driver side at an intersection while proceeding through on a green light. Claimant is not represented by counsel and was advised of the claims process.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the vehicle is listed under coverage that was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the policy records suggests the damage occurred before coverage began.

Entry 3: Claimant provided photos of the vehicle from the scene. The images confirm some of the details described, though they do not show the other vehicle's approach.

Entry 4: Sent a field inspection request for the damaged vehicle. Inspector noted damage to the driver door, quarter panel, and rear wheel area that is consistent with the described side impact.

Entry 5: Spoke with the claimant again to clarify the sequence of events. The account matched the initial report in every detail, including the direction of travel and the point of impact.

Entry 6: Reviewed the inspector's photos. A few older scratches appear along the lower door panel and may predate this loss. Will ask the appraiser to separate them from the new damage in the estimate.

Entry 7: Claimant reports neck pain and stiffness beginning the day after the collision. A neck strain is a plausible injury for a crash of this type. No prior injury to the neck or upper back has been reported or found in records checked so far.

Entry 8: Claimant is seeing a provider and has begun a standard course of treatment. Reviewed the treatment notes, which follow a usual course with symptoms easing as the claimant improved.

Entry 9: Asked the claimant where they were seated at impact. The answer was not fully clear and the details given still leave the seating position uncertain. Noted for follow-up.

Entry 10: No independent witnesses have come forward. The claim file relies on the claimant's statements, the photos, and the vehicle damage, which together are consistent with the reported impact.

Entry 11: Based on the current file, the claim appears to be progressing normally. Will continue to monitor treatment progress, complete the damage estimate, and follow up on the seating position question before final evaluation.
